references.text: Earlier in the same chapter, the Lord speaks to Moses and Aaron about separating themselves from the congregation, preparing for this direct speech to Moses.
The Lord speaks again to Moses after the judgment on Korah, using the same formula: 'The Lord spoke to Moses and said.'
The characteristic opening formula 'The Lord spoke to Moses' used consistently in Numbers to introduce divine instructions.
An early example of the same formula where the Lord speaks directly to Moses with instructions, establishing the pattern for divine communication.
The standard formula 'The Lord spoke to Moses and said' that introduces legislation and instructions in Leviticus.
